package_info.why_malicious: The package version contains multiple prototype pollution vulnerabilities that allow untrusted input to modify object prototypes, leading to potential arbitrary code execution or security bypasses. These vulnerabilities are exploitable when user-controlled input is passed to certain functions, making the package version dangerous in real-world applications.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives untrusted input as arguments to util.setProperty, which allows modification of the __proto__ property, resulting in prototype pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing user-controlled input to modify the __proto__ property can lead to prototype pollution, which attackers can exploit to alter application behavior or escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects input sanitization to prevent prototype modification; this code allows direct manipulation of object prototypes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use may involve setting object properties, but never __proto__ or similar prototype-related keys from untrusted sources.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives untrusted input as arguments to setParsedOption, which can be used to modify the __proto__ property, resulting in prototype pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Passing untrusted input to setParsedOption enables attackers to manipulate object prototypes, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or security bypass.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to restrict prototype-related keys from being set via user input; this code does not enforce such restrictions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Setting options on objects is common, but prototype keys should be filtered out.
key_indicators: Untrusted input used as property name

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code parses an untrusted .proto definition that can include prototype-polluting assignments, leading to prototype pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Parsing untrusted .proto definitions without sanitization allows attackers to inject prototype-polluting properties.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to validate and sanitize .proto definitions before parsing; this code does not.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parsing .proto files is legitimate, but only from trusted sources.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads an untrusted .proto file, which can contain prototype-polluting definitions, leading to prototype pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and parsing untrusted files without validation allows attackers to exploit prototype pollution vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to only load trusted .proto files or sanitize their contents.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Loading .proto files is normal, but only from trusted sources.

attack_chain.action: Attacker supplies untrusted input (arguments or files) to vulnerable protobufjs functions.
Prototype pollution alters application behavior or enables further exploitation (e.g., privilege escalation, arbitrary code execution).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full compromise of the application.

behavioral_signatures: Assignment to __proto__ or constructor.prototype via user input
Parsing or loading untrusted .proto files without sanitization
Untrusted input used as property names in object assignment
file_indicators: References to util.setProperty, ReflectionObject.setParsedOption, parse, or load in protobufjs
Untrusted .proto files being loaded or parsed
network_indicators: N/A (vulnerability is local, but exploitation may involve remote file or input delivery)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for usage of vulnerable protobufjs functions (util.setProperty, ReflectionObject.setParsedOption, parse, load) with untrusted input, especially where property names include '__proto__' or similar prototype-related keys. Flag any code paths where .proto files are loaded or parsed from untrusted sources. Use static analysis to detect assignment to prototype properties from user-controlled data.
